memos.risk:
Risk view on SLEUTHY, assuming the desk buys:

Pool depth is 185.8 SOL, which is workable for a $5-$10 ticket. Last-15-minute volume of about $327k is heavy, but net flow is only +65 SOL against 1,330 SOL sold, so the 53% return has been bought from late buyers. Launch bot present and a 0.81 sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes point to a fragile base.

Sane parameters if bought: $5 ticket, 25% stop from entry (the 22% drawdown from the 30-minute high means the stop should sit tight to that), 30-minute max hold.

Refuse any size if the pool drops below roughly 100 SOL, if a single seller takes more than 5% of the pool, or if price falls through the stop. My recommendation is to skip: this is a momentum-chasing setup with heavy distribution, and the base rate for buys this late after a parabolic move is poor.
memos.scout:
The case for buying is real but thin. The curve looks organic: bundle share is 4.7%, top-3 holders own 8.9%, and the completer share is 16.5%, so no single operator appears to control supply. Buyers number 214 on the curve, and in the last 15 minutes 1,305 wallets bought against 985 sellers, with net flow positive at +65 SOL and $327k in volume. The coin is up 3.3x over 30 minutes and only 22% off its high, so it has held most of its gains. Graduation took 487 seconds, which suggests real demand filled the curve.

Against that: the last 15 minutes show sell SOL nearly matching buy SOL (1,330 vs 1,396), and early post-graduation sells outnumber buys 0.81 to 1. A launch bot was present. Net flow is small relative to volume. Pool depth of 186 SOL means a $20 ticket will move little, but the round-trip cost is still 1.4-5.1%. I see no evidence of demand that will hold for the next 30-60 minutes beyond the momentum already priced in, so this does not clear the bar against a roughly 20% per-trade loss base rate. Skip, unless you want a tiny position on the thesis that the buyer count keeps climbing.
memos.skeptic: The most likely way this loses money is a distribution-into-strength exit. In the last 15 minutes, sellers (985) nearly matched buyers (1,305), and sell SOL (1,330) almost equaled buy SOL (1,396), so net flow of +65 SOL is thin for a coin that's up 3.3x. The 22% drawdown from the 30-minute high means the momentum is already fading. Early behavior is also weak: sell-to-buy ratio of 0.81 in the first two minutes after graduation, and a launch bot was present. Those point to sophisticated sellers taking profit on early buyers. Fees of 1.4-5.1% plus a $20 ticket leave little room for a 20%+ pullback to be survivable. Skip.
